claims.statement: Presentation shares SwiftUI forms/values while architecture tests ban native UI/storage/transport imports. Its operationConfirmation uses localized anchored SwiftUI confirmations or an app-injected centered renderer; Termind's UIKit renderer waits for presentation transitions and completes dismissal before executing actions.

Metrics centralizes desktop geometry. Host artwork uses bundled JSON with empty fallback, automatic distribution/related/Linux matching or explicit symbol/asset overrides; unknown overrides remain stored and render server fallback. Host color tags override brand tint then accent.

TFM uses semantic AppKit-backed colors and appearance-resolved native colors. Generic Highlight retains its accent wash, while Sidebar selection uses neutral primary fills at 10% key/6% inactive opacity, primary selected key-window text and accent leading icons, secondary inactive foregrounds and readable inline rename colors; the native menu outline remains accent-colored.

TFM explicit glass controls use system glass on macOS 26 with native material fallbacks, but the Sidebar column relies on NavigationSplitView's own background on macOS 26+ and adds only a pre-26 AppKit visual-effect fallback. Mobile cards retain conditional glass, dense-text backing and opaque/stronger-border accessibility fallbacks.

Standard mobile cards use 320-point minimum columns, 12-point gaps, 106-point minimum height and at most two Host tags. Opting-in collections use local mobile.compactCards for scaled compact columns capped at four and square-or-taller cards. Both modes force accessibility one-column layout; primary taps and secondary menus remain unchanged.

Shared Host sections and stateless HostEditorBindings bind platform-owned Host/custom-identity drafts and report creation callbacks without owning navigation or save policy. Desktop retains nested Vault editing and mobile retains a sheet-owned draft/save gate.

SingleLineTextInput preserves attributed paste while replacing newline runs and normalizes user-edit bindings without changing reads. Shared code delegates native paste/input through environment adapters supplied by each app rather than importing platform UI implementations.

AssistantTranscriptEntry shares stable timeline-derived typed rows and caller-supplied edit/fork eligibility, while desktop cached native ownership and mobile native-list environment/update handling remain distinct platform concerns.

UI visibility gates also control interaction/accessibility, motion helpers expose Reduce Motion policy, and adaptive tests cover language variants, native identity, focus and marked-text preservation rather than only final strings.

Adaptive mobile layouts preserve native children; desktop retains parked geometry and transcript-owner LRU. Mobile scene sessions own workspace intent/ordered presentation items; scene disconnection is not explicit discard.

Shared TerminalFontFields binds local preferences with an 8–36 range and macOS Slider/iOS Stepper. Catalogs include all loadable families including proportional fonts, sort locally and refresh on appearance/activation; unavailable choices remain stored while rendering resolves a copy.

TerminalFontSettings stores typography locally through AppStorage, separately from synchronized TerminalPreferences; TerminalSettingsModel persists preference edits before publishing and retains existing preferences on a save failure while exposing storageError.

Theme options read preferences/library without storage repair and show fallback notices. Rendering prepends local family with theme fallbacks and reset reinsertion, then manual size last. Desktop debounces drafts 300 ms and saves before navigation; invalid/deleted/failed drafts block navigation with discard/cancel, and discarded owners cannot autosave. Typing trailing spaces avoids name trimming. Both editors import UTF-8 and recover deleted themes as copies; mobile explicitly saves.

Desktop terminal tests cover family fallback/reset ordering, manual size precedence, controller identity, nonmutating theme fallback and zero writes opening Settings; the former mobile font rendering suite is not current coverage.

The Sidebar mode rail shares one glass capsule with neutral animated selection, explicit selected accessibility traits, Reduce Motion handling and key-window focus outline; the Assistant footer groups interactive New Chat/Archive glass controls on macOS 26+, using neutral Archive selection and a semibold primary glyph.

Desktop single-rule forwarding menus group Address and SSH Command in a Copy submenu, while mobile exposes flat copy actions before Edit/Duplicate; both use native pasteboards, disable unavailable SSH-command copying and leave forwarding execution to separate actions.

Standard snippet cards share adaptive metadata and reserved footer height; compact mobile cards use separate content retaining risk. Mobile taps open details and Run chooses missing targets and confirms destructive execution before its callback; desktop dispatches through its page owner.

Mobile Host cards activate through scene routing. Menus separate enabled SSH/SFTP, Telnet, Mosh and Eternal Terminal connections from Wake (when a Wake-on-LAN address exists), eligible Tailscale details, editing and deletion. Managed Hosts disable duplicate/delete; ordinary protocol-disabled Hosts retain edit/delete.

Mobile Host operations delegate connections to scene callbacks, editing to sheets and deletion to confirmation. Async duplication delegates to HostLibraryModel, re-reads and rejects managed sources, creates a new ID, clears custom SSH/Telnet and proxy identities and affected proxy usernames, resolves saving access and checks cancellation/source existence before saving. Desktop retains Quick Connect, Connect and Copy SSH Command.

MobileRootView binds the selected destination to a scene model and preserves one NavigationStack per registered feature inside a sidebar-adaptable TabView; adaptive tests assert the same native tab controller, five available tabs and scene/native selection with visible titles across compact and regular sizes and language/Dynamic Type variants.

MobileContentRegions subtracts active obstacles and uses a usable division only when both regions fit; MobilePaneLayout retains the same native children and last usable size while Assistant and Metrics gate obscured panels' hit testing and accessibility along with visibility.

Adaptive mobile tests verify native continuity beyond displayed strings: Metrics list identity, offset and selected page survive folds and vertical-menu transitions; Assistant transcript, composer focus and marked text survive divisions/occlusion; search, editor drafts and in-flight save feedback survive width changes.

Desktop workspace layout drag retains the native source pane mounted but omits it from temporary geometry; a pre-mounted native receiver checks current displayed workspace and matching pasteboard identity before preview/drop, splitting occupied pane edges or replacing empty slots, and rejects hidden destinations and unrelated drags.

Desktop Navigator layout drops use a native overlay on the List and measured global row frames to clamp pointer positions to Workspace insertion boundaries; preview geometry includes the dragged row while the move index excludes it, and valid Navigator drops reorder a workspace or detach a pane.

Vault presents MobileHostEditor as an item sheet with local draft and shared profile/connection fields and platform group/tag controls. Both editors disable managed Tailscale name/group, protocol and connection fields while retaining icon/tags/color and separate authentication username.

Mobile Host Save checks address, enabled protocol, enabled ports/transports, Wake-on-LAN validity, custom identities/proxies and SSH environment variables, bypassing ordinary custom SSH validation for managed Tailscale. Desktop also checks Wake-on-LAN validity, SFTP initial path and SSH route.

Mobile Host initialization loads custom identities once or a separate managed Tailscale username. Ordinary Save uses HostCustomIdentityDraft and the library; managed Save uses saveTailscaleHost. Child sheets feed selections and values into the parent.

MobileEditorSheet presents titleless discard confirmation for dirty Cancel and runs onCancel before clean/confirmed cancellation. Saving blocks editing/interactive dismissal, errors remain visible, disappearance cancels save and success checks cancellation before dismissing; a clean draft clears pending discard.

Desktop Find follows foreground destination/focused pane with Welcome content search and no custom-editor Find. Theme libraries keep a visible field; other slots use macOS 26 searchable or legacy native field/focus ownership with terminal navigation/cancellation callbacks.
Desktop toolbar creation actions derive from foreground destination rather than sidebar mode; Navigator native menus expose the same page verbs without first visiting the page.

Presentation leaves execution/replay data unchanged and projects live approval arguments separately from durable cards/model transcripts, with required projection failing closed. Ordinary JSON presenters receive failure state; knowledge tests reject success messages on failure. Previews preserve full projected items, desktop disclosure is keyed per card, and native plain detail values are selectable.

MobileCardTests checks the two-tag limit; current MobileCompactCardTests checks missing-credential warnings, forwarding state badges, snippet risk and localized Compact wording rather than geometry/persistence. MobileEditorToolbarTests covers localized Cancel, in-flight and failed Save, and More actions beside Save disabled during saving.

Shared AppStrings owns on-demand localized presentation resources for both apps; swiftUIKey preserves interpolation metadata and AppLocalization resolves native copy against the requested locale and app-bundle localization. Desktop offers Follow System and German, English, French, Japanese, Korean and both Chinese scripts with an AppleLanguages override and relaunch notice; Follow System removes the override. Mobile App settings has no equivalent language picker. Architecture tests reject app-local AppStrings and presentation-copy tests cover English, Japanese and both Chinese scripts.

The desktop Settings index offers App, Notifications, Terminal, Connections, AI and Sync category routes (Developer only in DEBUG); Logging is a separate optional debug entry, and Pro opens the paywall without adding a Settings category.

Desktop category/Logging routes parent to index, AI details to AI except provider models to provider, theme browsers/manager to Terminal and custom editor to manager. Back restores the displaced destination after index, falling back to Vault for a missing workspace.

Desktop Settings route/disappearance cleanup discards empty unconfigured providers except provider/model-list transitions, requires valid new MCP servers with lockable namespace, and retains skills with written content as drafts. Policy stays in the shell.

Mobile Settings uses a registered scene-owned tab with its own NavigationStack and native category NavigationLinks; the mobile paywall is a sheet controlled by app pro state rather than a desktop SettingsRoute destination.

Confirmation titles use LocalizedStringResource directly rather than swiftUIKey to avoid leaked interpolation metadata; the architecture test scans both apps, while mobile operationConfirmation explicitly resolves locale then passes verbatim dialog strings.

Mobile snippets call injected scene execution after target choice/risk confirmation. Sessions open one workspace per permitted Host using preferred terminal transport; snippet commands stay in live startup rather than restoration descriptors.

Both app settings shells expose NotificationSettingsFields for notification permissions and configuration, supplying the platform-specific open-settings action while maintaining independent desktop route and mobile native link navigation.

Desktop sidebar mode and visibility are window-scoped across destination changes; the mode rail reconciles destination and focused-pane changes, and a focused serial pane disables History, falling back to Snippets rather than activating it.

Desktop Snippets and History shelves host stable-ID SidebarListItem rows in an AppKit ListView; history rows keep identity across display changes and share a card height except for inline naming, which grows without changing ID.

The compact Snippets shelf persists expansion independently from the full Snippets page; collapsing removes rows without replacing the section header's identity, while the shelf's own footer search filters its sidebar list instead of the foreground titlebar Find query.
Desktop sidebar native row menus and blank-area menus have separate targets, so an empty-space right click does not invoke a row action.
Mobile Vault groups Hosts in collapsible sections and offers native feature links; search renders Host results and cross-feature links and can forward its query to their destination.

PresentationCopyTests verify resource resolution across English, Japanese and both Chinese scripts, nested native menu labels, plural/interpolated deletion messages and rendered SwiftUI text equivalence between resource and swiftUIKey via ImageRenderer.

Built-in selection saves a library selection without custom association when native themes are supported or selections exist; legacy selection saves name and disables overlay atomically. Named custom selection validates ID/appearance and associates the record. Browsers exit only after successful persistence and expose storageError otherwise.
Desktop theme search retains separate light/dark queries and custom-manager query; libraries keep visible toolbar Find even when empty, but custom editors and other Settings routes have no Find.

Native terminal menus localize editing and upload actions; iOS customizes both touch hooks with inline editing and Photos/Files groups. macOS adds Paste, Select All, Upload and optional Open with SFTP current/new workspace submenu alongside selected Copy. Upload and SFTP actions recheck availability.

Terminal Settings no longer exposes the retired synchronized keyword-highlighting editor. V52 removes historical highlighting preferences, while Settings preparation/legacy record handling excludes that inactive data and preserves other settings.

Local read_pane cards expose only terminal name and pane ID, with argument-ID fallback, suppress truncation notices and never fall through to raw output even for malformed or failed results; list_panes renders terminal rows with active/current badges.

The adaptive mobile workspace regression checks compact/regular restored workspace ordering, scene selection without duplication, native Back clearing selection, and Close All preserving connection history.

MobileNativeList separates layout-invalidating rowRevision updates from interactionRevision refreshes that retain mounted hosts and measured geometry; Assistant uses interaction revisions for streaming-dependent interactions. Mixed updates configure affected rows once and offscreen mounts use the latest renderer, with transcript tests asserting host identity, measurements, content size and history anchor preservation.

AgentToolPresentation accepts injected profiles and vocabulary; profiles override summaries, operations, batches, phases, details and truncation policy, distinguishing hidden details from fallback. Shared SwiftUI and native detail fields place secondary labels above values, omit empty value views, prioritize navigation over URLs, and color plain error values red without overriding message tints or link styling. AssistantToolDetails enables selection and renders retained items without folding; approval renders all projected arguments while only safety reasons fold. Compact wrappers own preview/full selection rather than the item renderer.

Trusted composition selects registered profiles by presenter ID with independent local pane/chat privacy, while MCP receives a default profile and decoded JSON falls back to generic structured items. An explicitly injected trusted presenter can supply typed items and layout; remote metadata cannot select local code.

Approval omits redundant host_id when a Host name is supplied; required argument projection fails closed to empty items without a presenter. Chat malformed, failed or missing-presenter details never fall back to raw bodies; matching Guardian denial output is suppressed as duplicate feedback.
